title: Assay (assay2chip stage S1)
description: What the source document says, still in lab language: the wet-lab steps in order, each quoted from the paper with the page it came from and how sure the extraction is. Written by assay2chip/stages/s1_*.py to assay2chip/work/<id>/assay.json. Every number here must be traceable to the source: anything the source did not state goes in `unresolved` instead of being filled in. Shape defined in assay2chip/README.md.

id.description: The run id, same as the work directory name (assay2chip/work/<id>/).

title.description: Title of the paper or protocol, as the source gives it.

placeholder.description: true while this file holds made-up steps rather than a real extraction.

extraction.description: S1's own provenance: which extractor ran (model or deterministic), why it fell back if it did, its confidence ceiling, counts and repairs. Open on purpose - S1 owns the shape - but it MUST say which mode produced the file, the same promise the `llm` block makes.

steps.description: The wet-lab steps in the order the source gives them, numbered from 1.

text.description: The sentence from the source, verbatim. Not a paraphrase: the rest of the pipeline cites it.

action.description: What the step does, in lab terms. S2 maps these onto canonical unit operations.

reagents.description: What goes in. Generic names only (wash_buffer, lysis_buffer): see CONFIDENTIALITY.md.

name.description: Generic reagent name, snake_case where possible. No vendors, catalogue numbers or prices.

volume_ul.description: Microlitres as stated by the source. null when the source gives no volume - and then say so in `unresolved`.

role.description: What the reagent is for; S2 uses it to pick a viscosity class.

target.description: What the step is done to, in the source's own words (the cells, the capsules, the supernatant).

duration_s.description: Seconds, as stated. null when the source gives no time.

temp_c.description: Degrees Celsius, as stated. null when the source gives no temperature (not 'room temperature' guessed as 22).

confidence.description: REQUIRED. How sure this step's fields are. 1.0 only when the source states every field outright; lower it for anything read between the lines. A guessed number presented as fact is the failure mode this whole repo fights, so any step below 1.0 should have a matching entry in `unresolved`.

quote_page.description: REQUIRED. Where in the source `text` came from: a page number, or a locator string for sources with no pages ('methods, para 3', 'line 412'). Never null - if it cannot be located, the step is not extracted.

notes.description: The ambiguity in this step, if any: what the source left open and how it was read.

note.description: Free comment on this entry (housekeeping; `notes` is the one about the source).

audit.description: How this step was read: why the confidence is what it is, the verbatim text behind each parsed number, a range the source gave instead of a value, whether the sentence was split or a repeat expanded. Open on purpose, and the right place for anything that would otherwise be a silent judgement call.

unresolved.description: REQUIRED, may be empty: every gap in the source. One entry per thing a later stage would otherwise have to invent (a volume, a time, a temperature, a particle size). Downstream stages carry these forward and the S10 report lists them.

step.description: The step the gap belongs to, or null when it is about the assay as a whole.

field.description: Which field is missing, e.g. volume_ul.

question.description: What is not known, in one sentence: 'volume not stated'.

assumed.description: The value a later stage used instead, if one was used. Always paired with `assumed_from`.

assumed_from.description: The contract key the assumed value came from, e.g. capsule.diameter_um. Never a bare literal.

audit.description: A deliberately OPEN object: the stage that wrote this file may show its working here in whatever shape suits it. Every other field in this contract is closed (additionalProperties: false), because a typo in a contract field is a bug; provenance is the one thing that must never be blocked by a schema, since a stage that cannot record how it reached a number tends to stop recording it at all. Nothing downstream may depend on the shape of this object.

source.description: Where the assay was read from, carried unchanged from S0 raw.json so every later file can be traced back to a document.

sha256.description: Hash of the bytes that were read, when the source is a local file.

retrieved_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp, for a DOI or URL.

llm.description: Which language-model mode produced this file. assay2chip/lib/llm.py fills it in; a stubbed result must never be mistakable for a real extraction.

mode.description: real: a model was called. stub: the deterministic offline fallback ran (tests, no network) - treat every number as made up. none: no model was involved.

model.description: Model id when mode is real.

tasks.description: The prompt task names that ran.
